MEMORANDUM

  Agenda Item #: _5_
  Meeting Date: March 12, 2020

TO:  HONORABLE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL

THRU:  KENNETH RUKAVINA, ACTING CITY MANAGER

FROM:  CARL MORITZ, URBAN FORESTER

SUBJECT: CONSIDERATION OF PARKLANDS COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATIONS OF
  MARCH 12, 2020

DATE:  APRIL 14, 2020

Issue/Purpose

The purpose of this memorandum is to transmit Parklands Committee recommendation for applications
from the March 12, 2020 meeting to the City Council.

Background/Discussion

At its meeting of March 12, 2020, the Parklands Committee reviewed five applications and discussed
four. The first item was a citizen application for a Change to Parklands. The second item was a citizen
application for tree removal to restore their neighbor’s view. The third item was a citizen application for
street tree removal for view restoration. Agenda item four, PC-533-20, was withdrawn in a phone voice
message by the applicant on March 9, 2020. The fifth item was a review of the designated street tree for
Cloyden Road.

1.  PC-CTP-12-20; Concept Plan for change to parklands to landscape a portion of the bluffs adjacent
  to Lunada Bay Elementary School from the end of phase 1-B to Via Alvarado

  Applicant:  Lunada Bay Homeowner Association
  1052 Via Palastra
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

Staff introduced this as a Concept Plan for a Change to Parklands. The application requests to remove
invasive weeds and non-native shrubs, install low growing native ground covers and add a stone-lined

  1
 decomposed granite trail in a 0.7 acre area located adjacent to Lunada Bay Elementary School. The trail
is proposed to end at the intersection of Via Alvarado and Paseo Del Mar. The Lunada Bay Homeowners
Association (LBHOA) will fund the project through private donations and grants with an estimated cost
of $45,000. Volunteers will provide maintenance for three years or until the plants are established and
will remove plants unsuccessful or too tall. The City is requested to provide deliveries of rocks and mulch
and to provide water. The City gave public notice 20 days in advance with three public notice boards at
the site and three public notice boards adjacent to Phase 1 of the Beautify Lunada Bay (BLB) project.

Bill Alior, of the LBHOA, provided a PowerPoint presentation. Mr. Alior thanked Phase I volunteers for
their efforts and indicated plans for Phase II were modified from lessons learned from Phase I. The
irrigations system is reduced to hose bibs every 50 feet, no grading is proposed and all planting and
maintenance is to be performed by volunteers. Two palettes of native low growing shrubs and grasses are
proposed. The path is proposed as an alternative to walking in the street or in the weeds and mud.

The LBHOA indicated public outreach to 222 home with 38 positive responses. The LBHOA conducted
a community meeting with 25 attendees on October 23, 2019. Comments at the meeting were mixed.

Megan Wolft and John Horne of the Palos Verdes Peninsula Land Conservancy and Marlene Breen and
Edward Deason, members of the LBHOA, N. J. Jaeger a volunteer, spoke in support of the project. They
indicated the project is environmentally responsible and a benefit for the community.

Barbara Hauser and Roge Ramsy of Rocky Point Road spoke in opposition to the project. They indicated
the area didn’t need restoration, the project lacked broad support, the Parklands are for parks, the native
plants will become a fire hazard and the decomposed granite paths are too narrow and restricted where
people and pets can walk. Barbara. Hauser indicated the public meeting at the school was attended by
resident that mostly didn’t support the project.

The Committee complemented the LBHOA for Phase 1 of the BLB project and indicated it was very
attractive. One member of the Committee asked about the fire hazard potential of low growing native
plants compared to the typical stands of mustard. The Forester indicated the mustard has more potential
as fuel but once the City mows the weeds it is less fuel than the native plants.

The Committee agreed the project would be a benefit but needed to be modified to address the comments
expressed by the residents. The unnatural decomposed granite path needs to be modified to a meandering
and unrestrictive trail through a meadow of native grasses. The use of rock also needs to be reduced and
less like a formal park.

Action: Committee member Richie-Bray motioned second by Cooper to recommend to the City
Council approval with modification. Modify the decomposed granite path to an informal and less
restrictive meandering natural trail through a meadow of grasses, reduce the use of rock, increase
the use of native grasses, and submit a new Concept Plan to the Parklands Committee. The vote
was (5-0, in favor).

2.  PC-531-20; Application to remove one Rusty Leaf Fig tree located in the parkway adjacent to
  1400 Chelsea Road.

  Applicant:  Marlene Breene
  2325 Palos Verdes Drive West #212
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

  2
 Staff introduced this application as a request to remove one Rusty Leaf Fig tree to protect the existing
view of the adjacent neighbor at 1404 Apsely Road. The unpermitted and nonconforming Fig has been
repetitively topped at 15 feet above grade by the previous resident to keep below their neighbors view
and a new landscape is proposed to be installed below the tree. Staff also indicate the fig was root invasive
and drops large amounts of fruit onto the street if not trimmed.

The applicant was concerned with view restoration and indicated any tree above 10 feet tall would
encroach into the view of her client and for their neighbor.

The Committee were not in agreement concerning the Fig’s view encroachment. They all agreed it was
not the neighborhood character or the designated street tree. One member indicated the tree was not
currently encroaching into the view and could be maintained.

Action: Committee member Cooper motioned second by Groves to recommend approval to the
City Council to remove one Rusty Leaf Fig tree located adjacent to 1400 Chelsea Road according
to the ‘Standard Conditions For Tree Removal Approvals’. Require a $500 payment to the ‘Tree
Bank’ and removal of the stump. The vote was (4-0-1, in favor, Richie-Bray dissenting).

3.  PC-532-20; Application to remove one Aleppo pine tree located in the parkway adjacent to 1217
  Via Romero

  Applicant:  John Phippen
  2505 Via Olivera
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

Staff introduced this application to remove one Aleppo pine tree as a request to restore the view. Staff
indicated the Aleppo pine was once the designated street tree for Via Romero but was changed in 1994
by the Parklands Committee following Resolution No. R92-66, which eliminated future planting of most
pine trees in the public areas. The neighborhood character is Aleppo pines but most of these pines on Via
Romero in the parkway below properties on Via Olivera have been topped for the view without permits.

The applicants indicated they had purchased this home 35 years ago for the view and that they are seeking
to restore a portion of that view. The Pippen’s communicated with the owner of 1217 Via Romero, Kelly
Sampson, and provide a letter with her support.

The Committee agreed the pine was a large and dense view obstruction but also the neighborhood
character. When Committee member Groves began to comment it became apparent his home was within
500 feet of the tree in the application and recused himself and left the room. The balance of neighborhood
character and view restoration was the focus of the other four members.

Action: Committee member Cooper motioned second by McCabe to recommend approval to the
City Council to remove one Aleppo pine tree located in the parkway adjacent to 1217 Via Romero
according to the ‘Standard Conditions For Tree Removal Approvals’. Require a $500 payment to
the ‘Tree Bank’ and removal of the stump. The vote was (3-1-1, in favor, Richie-Bray dissenting,
Groves recused).

  3
 4.  Consideration of a new designated street tree for Cloyden Road.

Staff introduced this item as a re-designation of the designated street tree for Cloyden Road. A history of
the process and criteria for tree selection were presented. A slide show was presented along with the three
suggested options with pictures.

There were no resident attending the meeting for this item. The Committee agreed the Weeping
Bottlebrush was the tree most in character with the Red Iron Bark Eucalyptus weeping canopies.

Action: Committee member Richie-Bray motioned second by Cooper to recommend the Weeping
Bottlebrush tree as the new ‘Designated Street Tree’ for Cloyden Road. The vote was (5-0, in favor).

Notification

Interested parties attending the Parklands Committee meeting were made aware that the above noted
recommendations would be transmitted to the City Council. This item is also noticed in the standard
manner for City Council meetings.

Alternatives Available to the City Council

City Council has the option to approve, deny, amend or remand this item to the Parklands Committee.
Should the City Council consider amending and have its own hearing on this item, it is recommended
that the discussion be calendared for a future meeting so appropriate notice can be assured.

Recommendation

It is recommended that the City Council review and approve the Parklands Committee recommended
actions of March 12, 2020.
